chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: Harris's singing power
summary: Harris was the first to dance on his heels and as loud as a six-piece band when amplified; Durham played guitar in that band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, he -- I don't know Chris, we weren't here then. But he must have been about the hottest blues singer in the country for several years.
And he could really sing, you know?
The blues -- wasn't nobody who could sing like him, not out like that. He was as loud as a six-piece band when he was amplified. He could ring a house.
Well, it seems like Good Morning, Judge and Bloodshot Eyes, --
He's the first guy and he was dancing on his heels all the time, bouncing and rocking. Break up the audience.
Did you have a good guitar player in that band?
No, I played the guitar at that time.
I was trying to think of some of the guys he was out with and I can't think of their names.
